name: David Vance
fact: Vance won the autumn 1977 election he had campaigned for as freshman president, and ASG president Bob Moore rebuked him for spending $192 on the campaign. The campaign itself ran two supporters through Bowling Green in a 1948 Plymouth dressed as gangsters, with a WANTED poster carrying his photograph taped to the car door.

src.label: 1978 Talisman, p. 34, captions to the ASG section

name: David Carwell
fact: As activities vice president Carwell set out the three tests an outside concert promoter had to meet before ASG would deal with it: an office within 500 miles of Western, at least 75 major concerts promoted, and at least $2 million grossed on them. He said Sunshine Promotions of Indianapolis met all three. The contract was never signed, and the bond dispute broke shortly before the Player and Exile concert of 3 November.

name: David Young
fact: The constitution the student body approved at the April 1979 general election broke the representative-at-large election into 24 separate races for the 24 seats. Young, as administrative vice president, said the point was to force competition between candidates rather than let them run as a field. The 1979 Talisman's index gives his full name as David Paul Young.

name: Alan Reid
fact: A year before his term as senior class president Reid was a Bowling Green junior working as a state administrative intern, and a member of Pi Sigma Alpha, the political science honour society, which he credited with helping him settle into the job. He told the Talisman he was heading for a career in politics.

name: Steve Shipp
fact: Shipp was a Hopkinsville student, a senior by 1979-80, and a member of Lambda Chi Alpha.

name: Anne Mckee
fact: McKee was a junior from Anderson, Indiana, and president of Alpha Xi Delta in the year she sat in ASG. Under her the chapter sang at the Colonial Nursing Home, raised money for the Wee Care Center and took children from Kinder Kollege to a fire station.

name: David Sturgeon
fact: Sturgeon was a Louisville junior, president of Sigma Nu, and one of the twelve members of the Interfraternity Council in the year he sat in ASG. He had chaired the Interfraternity Council itself the year before, as a sophomore.

name: Perry Hines
fact: Hines sat on the Interhall Council as well as in ASG in 1980-81; both bodies were photographed on the same page of the Talisman and he appears in each.

name: Mark Chesnut
fact: In the year he was ASG treasurer Chesnut won the men's intramural badminton singles and, with Mitch Gum, the racquetball doubles, both for Sigma Alpha Epsilon. The Talisman's champion lists print his surname Chestnut; its index files him as Chesnut, Mark Cameron. He was an accounting major.
